levels.title: LASA Pair Familiarization
levels.description: Recognize common look-alike and sound-alike brand/generic pairs from visual prompts.
levels.learningObjective: Identify documented LASA counterparts and recognize why similar orthography leads to dispensing confusion.

activities.learningObjective: Identify documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike medication counterparts from verified ISMP pairs.

questions.prompt: Which medication is a documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike counterpart to Abelcet?
questions.explanation: Abelcet (amphotericin B lipid complex) is frequently confused with conventional amphotericin B. Mix-ups between formulations can cause severe dosing and toxicity errors.

questions.prompt: Accupril (quinapril) is commonly confused with which medication due to phonetic and orthographic similarity?
questions.explanation: Accupril (an ACE inhibitor for hypertension) and Aciphex (rabeprazole, a PPI for acid reflux) look and sound similar, despite having completely different therapeutic indications.

levels.title: Tall Man Lettering Discrimination
levels.description: Differentiate look-alike generic medications using capitalized Tall Man letter patterns.
levels.learningObjective: Recognize and interpret ISMP/FDA Tall Man lettering to disrupt orthographic confusion between look-alike names.

activities.learningObjective: Construct verified Tall Man capitalization to distinguish high-risk look-alike medication pairs.

questions.prompt: Convert this drug name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: acetaZOLAMIDE capitalizes ZOLAMIDE to emphasize differences from acetaminophen and acetoHEXAMIDE.

questions.prompt: Convert this drug name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: acetoHEXAMIDE capitalizes HEXAMIDE to distinguish this sulfonylurea antidiabetic from acetaZOLAMIDE.

questions.prompt: Convert this drug name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: predniSONE capitalizes SONE to distinguish it from the closely related corticosteroid prednisoLONE.

levels.title: LASA Distinction & Situational Recognition
levels.description: Distinguish easily confused medication names and apply recognition in dispensing scenarios.
levels.learningObjective: Distinguish between confusable LASA pairs and recognize target medications in realistic prescription contexts.

activities.learningObjective: Differentiate subtle orthographic and phonemic differences between look-alike drug names.

questions.prompt: A prescription is requested for acetazolamide. Which of these look-alike medications is the correct Tall Man representation to prevent mix-ups?
questions.explanation: acetaZOLAMIDE capitalizes ZOLAMIDE to clearly distinguish it from acetoHEXAMIDE.

activities.learningObjective: Recognize the correct medication name in a realistic dispensing verification context.

questions.scenario: A patient presents a written prescription order for Accupril. The dispensary shelf stores multiple medications with similar phonemic and visual names.
questions.prompt: Which medication name matches the prescription order and avoids a look-alike mix-up with Aciphex?
questions.explanation: Accupril must be distinguished from Aciphex to prevent dispensing confusion.

levels.title: Unit 1 Mastery
levels.description: Comprehensive review and unassisted Tall Man lettering mastery for Unit 1.
levels.learningObjective: Demonstrate complete unit mastery of LASA distinction and unassisted Tall Man lettering without prompts or scaffolding.

activities.learningObjective: Review distinguishing differences between high-risk look-alike oral agents before unassisted recall.

questions.prompt: Which medication name correctly applies ISMP Tall Man lettering to prevent confusion between acetohexamide and acetazolamide?
questions.explanation: acetoHEXAMIDE capitalizes HEXAMIDE to distinguish this sulfonylurea antidiabetic from the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor acetaZOLAMIDE.

activities.learningObjective: Independently construct the exact Tall Man lettering for prednisone without scaffolding.

questions.prompt: UNIT MASTERY CAPSTONE TASK: Type the complete drug name using correct Tall Man lettering (capitalizing the specific distinguishing letters):
questions.explanation: predniSONE capitalizes SONE to prevent mix-ups with the look-alike corticosteroid prednisoLONE.
